learning_objective: 🧬 Decode the blueprint of life! Explore the Human Genome Project, DNA fingerprinting, and the revolutionary gene-editing tool CRISPR-Cas9.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A massive 13-year international project (1990-2003) to sequence all 3.2 billion base pairs in human DNA. It revealed that humans have about 20,000-25,000 genes, and surprisingly, 99.9% of our DNA is identical in all humans!

Sanger sequencing (first generation) reads DNA bases one by one using chain-terminating nucleotides. Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) is modern technology that sequences millions of fragments simultaneously, making it incredibly fast and cheap.
Sequencing the genome created so much data that it couldn't be analyzed manually. Bioinformatics merges biology, computer science, and IT to store, retrieve, and analyze immense genomic data.

Derived from a bacterial immune system, CRISPR uses a 'guide RNA' to find a very specific sequence of DNA, and the 'Cas9' enzyme cuts it exactly there. Scientists can use this to delete disease-causing genes or insert healthy ones with pinpoint accuracy.

Developed by Alec Jeffreys. It relies on 'Variable Number of Tandem Repeats' (VNTRs) in our junk DNA. The number of these repeats is highly unique to each individual, making it perfect for forensic science and paternity testing.

fun_activity.title: 💻 The Data Mountain
fun_activity.instructions: If you wanted to print the entire human genome sequence (A, T, C, G) into books, with each page holding 1000 letters and each book having 1000 pages, you would need 3,300 books just to print the sequence of one single human cell!

exam_tips: 📌 Chromosome 1 has the most genes (2968), and the Y chromosome has the fewest (231). This is a frequent objective question.
📌 Understand the principle of DNA fingerprinting: It relies on DNA polymorphism (variation at the genetic level) observed in non-coding repetitive DNA.
📌 CRISPR stands for Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats. Know its origin (bacterial defense against viruses).
quick_recap: ⭐ Less than 2% of the human genome actually codes for proteins; the rest is regulatory or 'junk' DNA.
⭐ The Human Genome Project was called a 'Mega Project' due to its scale, cost, and international collaboration.
⭐ Southern Blotting is the technique used to transfer separated DNA fragments from a gel to a nylon membrane during DNA fingerprinting.
